reader.requirement: At --std 85 the compiler must refuse a PAGE HEADING or PAGE FOOTING report group (either spelling) in a report whose RD has no PAGE clause, and accept it when the PAGE clause is written (a 1985 PAGE clause always carries integer-1, so a PAGE clause always defines the page limit).
reader.edition-search: Read BindGroupType and the PAGE-clause arm that sets ReportModel.Paged (set when page.integerOperand() is written): no CobolVersion, EditionInfo or ConstructRegistry test on either; Edition.Error only records. A PAGE clause without integer-1 is refused by the parser at 85 (COBOL5506), so Paged equals 'a PAGE clause is specified' at this edition.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: 2023 SR12 adds the OR PAGE phrase and states 'a PAGE clause that defines the page limit'; at 85 OR PAGE does not exist (refused COBOL0900) and every PAGE clause defines the limit, so the same test is exact.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: witnesses cover a page heading without PAGE; a page footing without PAGE and the legal page footing with PAGE were probed here.

reader.notes: BindGroupType refuses PH/PF when the RD is not paged, at every edition. The message names the enum (TYPE PageHeading) and cites §2023:13.18.57.3 SR12 rather than the 1985 rule; cosmetic only.

refuter.evidence: Read the PAGE-clause arm of ResolveReports that sets ReportModel.Paged (line 219) and BindGroupType's PH/PF refusal; Paged is per model. Probe phleak.cob at --std 85: R1 paged with a PH, R2 with no PAGE clause and a PF: R2's PF refused COBOL0899 'RD R2: TYPE PageFooting requires a PAGE clause' (plus COBOL2199 for its relative LINE), R1 untouched, so a paged RD earlier in the section does not license a later unpaged one. tworpt.cob: PH and PF in two paged reports accepted and presented.
